The proposed answer is wrong. The correct value is 100.

The error is the step where the integral becomes $\int_{-9}^{11}(9w+5)\,dw$. The substitution $y = g(x)$ gives $dy = g'(x)\,dx$, so the integrand must keep the factor $g'(x)$.

Since $g(-1) = -9$ and $g(1) = 11$, the limits become $x = -1$ to $x = 1$:

$$\int_{-9}^{11} f(y)\,dy = \int_{-1}^{1} (9x+5)\,g'(x)\,dx, \qquad g'(x) = 7x^6 + 30x^4 + 9x^2.$$

The term $9x\,g'(x)$ is odd, so it integrates to 0 over $[-1, 1]$. The remaining term gives

$$\int_{-1}^{1} 5\,g'(x)\,dx = 5\big(g(1) - g(-1)\big) = 5(11 + 9) = 100.$$

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
